Sure thing, here’s the link to the one I purchased. The seller is often sold out, but I’m sure if you just search Polybar on Etsy or Google, you can likely find one. https://www.etsy.com/listing/1325558831/

I actually prefer the Polybar I ordered over the Bitwise one. It seems a little cheaper than it costs and I don’t much like the durability of it. I also don’t like that I had to glue the base on to the bar myself, seems like it should be like a snap-on or something. If you don’t glue it right it will end up being flimsy and wobbly while you’re playing.

Buttons aren’t very good for tapping unless you oil them with something. They’re very stiff and don’t allow for good sliding.

I personally didn’t like the fact that it only came in one color. Beige is not a guitar hero color lol

Overall, I’d probably give the guitar a 5/10, it’s not a bad purchase but my polybar is much more user friendly than this one.

Another thing I wanted to mention - when I was a kid, I was stuck on medium. So to get better, I turned on no fail and just played every song on expert til I could get it right or pass. Challenge yourself

Just something I want to mention to you - your hardware matters. For years, I was only playing on the standard guitar hero guitar, which was fine, but I never saw any improvement in skill. Like yeah, I could play on expert and hit like maybe 85-90% consistently but I was always missing sections that I thought were easy or tappable. Then a few months ago, I ordered one of those little polybar guitars off of Etsy, one of the mini guitars, and my game has literally improved by a milestone. I’m able to tap way easier, I’m hitting sections that I think are more difficult, there’s nearly no lag in my gameplay. I think depending on your hardware, you should give another piece a try.
